small_guidance: Move the IC loop to the OUTERMOST position and the kd/kh/kw loops inside; precompute the IC-strided x base offset once per ic. Also, hoist invariant pointer math (id_*IH*IW + ih_*IW + iw_ etc.) out of the inner kernel loop, and use BLOCK_OC=32, BLOCK_SP=64, num_warps=4, num_stages=2 as the safe baseline. Reduce register pressure (currently 123 regs/thread → only 16% occupancy) by using smaller accumulator tiles like (BLOCK_SP=32, BLOCK_OC=32) and adding configs with num_warps=2.
large_guidance: Redesign the conv_transpose3d as an im2col-style GEMM where the K-dimension is IC*KD*KH*KW and one program computes a tile of (BLOCK_M output spatial positions × BLOCK_N output channels) using tl.dot. The current scalar outer-product accumulation (acc += x[:,None]*w[None,:]) inside a triple-nested kd/kh/kw/ic loop produces extreme register pressure (123 regs/thread, 16.7% theoretical occupancy) and makes the kernel compute-bound at 95% SOL despite low DRAM use. Use channels-last input layout so IC is the contiguous K-axis, and gather the input via index math from (od+PD-kd)/SD with validity masks. Fold BN affine and the spatial-mean subtraction's first pass into the conv epilogue (write y and accumulate per-(N,C) sum atomically or in a second small kernel) to eliminate the extra 700MB read/write of fused_bn_submean.
